description: MAP-Elites looks for many good solutions that behave differently, not for one best solution (*quality diversity*). The user gives a few behaviour measures (*descriptors*), and the algorithm splits their range into a grid of cells; each cell keeps its cheapest solution so far, its *elite*. Each step picks a random elite, changes it by crossover with a second elite and by mutation (each with a set probability), and puts the child into the cell of its descriptor if that cell is empty or the child is strictly cheaper. The result is a map of the best cost found in each region of behaviour, for example plans that differ in length and risk. It gives no optimality guarantee for any cell; more evaluations fill and improve more cells.

papers.title: Illuminating search spaces by mapping elites
